correctness.rationale: For common \(k,N\), HHI ordering is exactly the ordering of \(Q=\sum_i n_i^2\), while Hall–Tideman ordering is the reverse ordering of \(R=\sum_i i d_i\) for descending sizes. Two independently generated complete profile sets agree, and exact comparison of all \(762\) admissible pairs proves weak agreement through \(N=9\), the unique tie split at \(10\), no strict reversal through \(11\), and exactly one strict reversal at \(12\).

value.rationale: HHI is a standard concentration benchmark, while Hall–Tideman deliberately replaces share self-weighting with rank weighting and incorporates all firms. Fixing firm count and total isolates that design difference. The exact first strict reversal and its unique sharp witness provide a natural interpretation and implementation benchmark rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
